newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait could tell nationals to chip in for health.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait could tell nationals to chip in for health.

text.p: Kuwait could oblige native workers and their employers to shoulder some of the costs of state health services, an official said on Monday.
"It is some form of an insurance plan," a health ministry official told Reuters. "The issue is under study. It has to be approved by the cabinet and the national assembly (parliament)."
According to the envisaged plan Kuwaiti workers, their employers and the state would be required to contribute varied amounts to the scheme, he said.
The ministry is discussing the details of the measure with local insurance firms, he added.
Currently the 720,000-strong native population receives health care services free of charge, while some 1.25 million expatriates pay token fees on some medical services.

The Gulf state, which spends about $900 million annually on health services, has announced plans to impose compulsory health insurance on its foreign residents to cut costs in what it sees as excessive use of health care services.
Kuwaitis do not pay taxes and they enjoy a wide range of free or heavily subsidised state services.
